variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high fidelity concept render of a native Android mobile DJ application, visual direction A: Precision Atelier.
Primary request: liquid glass meets restrained steampunk, optimized to look like a professional touch-first live DJ instrument. This is a visual concept for a new product, not an existing DJ brand.
Composition: one wide 20:9 landscape phone display, viewed straight on with no perspective distortion, occupying almost the entire wide canvas. Very slim black device bezel, neutral dark studio backdrop, no hands, no external equipment. Small presentation label outside screen at upper left: "A — PRECISION ATELIER".
Exact common screen layout: thin top status bar showing "USB MASTER + CUE", small "REC" and small "ParDay" access button at top right. Two compact horizontal full-width waveform lanes, cyan Deck A above orange Deck B. Below them Deck A left and Deck B right, each with fictional track name, 124.0 BPM and 8A, a large shallow circular jog control, "SYNC", four numbered hot cue pads, large separate "CUE" and play buttons. Left track "AURORA DRIVE"; right track "COPPER SKY". Compact central mixer with two channel faders, gain and filter dials, readable meter ladders. Crossfader lower centre. Bottom workspace tabs: "LIBRARY", "PADS", "FX", "STEMS". Tiny "CONCEPT" indicator. Everything meticulously aligned with large mobile touch targets and restrained professional control density.
Palette/materials: deep graphite #0C1015, smoked translucent glass surfaces #171D26, bright warm-white text, champagne brass #B9955D on precision-machined jog rims and selected dial details; subtle knurling and instrument engravings; cyan #53D7E8 Deck A, warm orange #FF955A Deck B. Glossy liquid-glass edges and soft refraction on small surfaces; solid opaque surfaces under critical text and faders. Steampunk expressed as elegant engineered brass and tactile instrument detailing, never theatrical gears or pipes.
Typography: exceptionally crisp modern sans serif labels, tabular numeric readouts, hierarchy that reads from waveforms to track status to transport. Product-grade render, handsome machining, highly readable professional UI.
Constraints: no app product name; ParDay is only the small AI assistant button, not product branding. No marketing slogans, no wall of decorative cards, no exposed cogs, no steam, no Victorian ornaments, no headphones/cables, no neon cyberpunk, no desktop mouse UI. Do not imply all professional modules fit at once; show only the performance workspace. No text outside specified labels except tiny needed control labels.
